chunks: And in the narration of al-Sakūnī, he said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said:
If a woman says, 'My husband is to me as the back of my mother,' then there is no expiation upon her.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.السَّكُونِيِّ: al-Sakūnī, the narrator through whom this report is transmitted
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman or wife mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.كَظَهْرِ أُمِّي: a formula of comparison associated with ẓihār
key_terms.كَفَّارَةَ: expiation required for certain legally consequential acts

ai.seo_question: If a woman declares her husband like the back of her mother, is expiation required upon her?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ẓihār when uttered by a woman regarding her husband. It states that such a statement does not entail kaffārah upon her, indicating that the legal consequence of ẓihār does not apply in this form to the wife.
